headlines.title: Paramount paid Netflix $2.8 billion to walk away from its $82.7-billion Warner Bros. deal — and Netflix stock jumped 14%
headlines.summary: You could see the results of this deal show up in your portfolio — or your streaming bill.

headlines.title: Netflix's Newest Rival Has Nearly $70 Billion in Annual Sales. It Also Carries About $82 Billion of Debt.
headlines.summary: The merged Paramount and Warner Bros. now outsells the top streamer by around a third. Should shareholders worry?

headlines.title: Skydance Sinks 8% a Day After Completing Warner Bros. Discovery Acquisition; Netflix Holds Flat, Walt Disney Slips
headlines.summary: Skydance just closed the deal everyone was watching, and the market responded by punishing the buyer. Whether that selloff reflects a debt problem or a passing reaction depends on what happens next with the integration.

headlines.title: Netflix Stock Plunges 26.8% Year to Date: 3 Key Reasons to Stay Away
headlines.summary: NFLX's slowing growth, rising content costs and premium valuation amid fierce streaming competition make the stock one to avoid for now.

headlines.summary: These growing businesses are trading at reasonable valuations.

description: Netflix, Inc. provides entertainment services worldwide. The company offers television (TV) series, documentaries, feature films, games, and live programming across various genres and languages. It also provides members the ability to receive streaming content through a host of internet-connected devices, including TVs, digital video players, TV set-top boxes, and mobile devices. Netflix, Inc. was incorporated in 1997 and is headquartered in Los Gatos, California.
